mainEntity.name: Does trade-in value reduce sales tax?

acceptedAnswer.text: In most US states, yes — sales tax is calculated on the price after subtracting your trade-in value, not the full vehicle price.

mainEntity.name: Should I include destination or dealer fees?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — enter them in the Dealer Fees, Title & Documentation field (or add them to the vehicle price). They're typically rolled into the loan, so leaving them out understates the amount financed.

mainEntity.name: Is it better to lease or finance a car?

acceptedAnswer.text: Financing builds equity and has no mileage limits, while leasing typically offers lower monthly payments but no ownership at the end — the right choice depends on how long you keep vehicles and how much you drive.

mainEntity.name: How much should my down payment be?

acceptedAnswer.text: 20% is a common guideline for new cars and 10% for used, though any amount that avoids being 'underwater' (owing more than the car's worth) as it depreciates is reasonable.

mainEntity.name: Should I choose a shorter or longer auto loan term?

acceptedAnswer.text: Shorter terms (36-48 months) minimize total interest and reduce the risk of owing more than the car is worth, while longer terms lower the monthly payment at a higher total cost.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth negotiating the vehicle price separately from financing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — negotiating price and financing separately, rather than focusing only on the monthly payment, generally leads to a better overall deal since dealers can adjust either variable to hit a target monthly number.

mainEntity.name: Does a manufacturer rebate lower my sales tax too?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on your state. Most states tax the vehicle's full pre-rebate price, so a rebate lowers your loan amount but not your tax bill. A handful of states (including Arizona, Iowa, Kansas, Minnesota, Missouri, Nebraska, Texas, and Wyoming) tax the post-rebate price instead.
